title: AI learning route
subtitle: From prompting basics to team guidance: evaluation, agents and privacy, using free resources.

stages.title: Prompting basics
stages.goal: Get reliable answers from a model by writing clear prompts. Everything later builds on this.

gate.build: Write five prompts for tasks you do every week, such as a status summary, risk wording or a stakeholder reply. Note what makes each answer better or worse.
gate.check: Can you say in one sentence why a clearer prompt gave a better answer?

resources.title: Interactive prompt engineering tutorial
resources.note: Hands-on notebooks that teach prompting one technique at a time.

resources.title: Anthropic courses
resources.note: Anthropic's educational courses, including one on real-world prompting.

stages.title: AI evaluation
stages.goal: Measure whether an AI answer is good, with repeatable tests instead of gut feel.

gate.build: Write a 10-case suite from your own work, run it on two models, and compare them in the HTML report from your toolkit.
gate.check: Which of your checks would let a wrong answer pass? Which would fail a right one?

resources.title: Define success criteria and build evaluations
resources.note: Anthropic's guide to writing measurable success criteria and test cases.

resources.title: Your AI product needs evals
resources.note: A practitioner's essay on building evals for an AI product.

resources.title: Evaluating AI agents (DeepLearning.AI)
resources.note: Beginner short course built with Arize AI: about 2.5 hours, 15 video lessons, basic Python needed.
resources.cost: Free to enrol during the platform beta. The graded assignment and certificate need a paid membership.

resources.title: Inspect AI tutorial
resources.note: Write and run your first eval with the UK AI Security Institute's framework.

resources.title: Your own toolkit: 02-ai-eval-toolkit
resources.note: The modular Python toolkit from this repo. Extend it as you learn.

resources.title: AI evals: everything you need to know
resources.note: Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar answer common eval questions, such as how many examples you need.

resources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
resources.note: Anthropic's engineering write-up on evaluating agents.

resources.title: Inspect AI
resources.note: Open-source framework for LLM evaluations from the UK AI Security Institute.

resources.title: Inspect Evals
resources.note: A collection of ready-made evals for Inspect AI. Good for reading how others write them.

resources.title: promptfoo
resources.note: Tests prompts, agents and RAG setups, and also does red teaming. Declarative configs, command line and CI support.

resources.title: DeepEval
resources.note: Python framework for evaluating LLM outputs.

resources.title: Ragas
resources.note: Evaluation toolkit for LLM applications, known for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) checks.

resources.title: lm-evaluation-harness
resources.note: Framework for evaluating language models on standard academic benchmarks.

resources.title: OpenAI Evals
resources.note: A framework for evaluating LLMs, plus an open-source registry of benchmarks.

stages.title: Agents
stages.goal: Understand how models use tools to complete multi-step tasks, and when a simple workflow is the better choice.

gate.build: Build a small agent with two or three tools, for example one that reads a risk log and drafts a status note. Then add test cases for it to your eval suite.
gate.check: When would a fixed workflow beat an agent for this task?

resources.title: Building effective AI agents
resources.note: Anthropic's guide to agent design patterns.

resources.title: Hugging Face AI agents course
resources.note: Theory to hands-on building, with smolagents, LlamaIndex and LangGraph. Units, three bonus units and an optional certificate.

resources.title: AI agents for beginners (Microsoft)
resources.note: A lesson-by-lesson open course with code samples.

resources.title: What is the Model Context Protocol?
resources.note: The open protocol for connecting AI apps to tools and data.

resources.title: Writing effective tools for AI agents
resources.note: How to design the tools an agent calls.

resources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
resources.note: How to manage what an agent sees as its task grows.

resources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
resources.note: A real multi-agent system, described by the team that built it.

resources.title: MCP Python SDK
resources.note: Documentation for building your own MCP server in Python.

stages.title: Privacy and security
stages.goal: Know what personal data can reach an AI tool, what the law expects, and how models get attacked.

gate.build: Add a privacy red-team suite to your toolkit: prompts that try to pull out personal data or hidden instructions. Try Presidio as a stronger replacement for the no_pii check.
gate.check: What personal data could reach an AI tool in your team's daily work, and where does it go next?

resources.title: ICO guidance on AI and data protection
resources.note: The UK regulator's guidance on applying data protection law to AI.

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications
resources.note: The standard list of security risks for LLM applications, such as prompt injection.

resources.title: Microsoft Presidio
resources.note: Open-source tool that finds and masks personal data in text, images and structured data.

resources.title: ICO: explaining decisions made with AI
resources.note: How to explain AI-assisted decisions to the people they affect.

resources.title: ICO audit toolkit: governance and accountability in AI
resources.note: A checklist-style view of what good AI governance looks like to an auditor.

resources.title: NCSC guidelines for secure AI system development
resources.note: UK National Cyber Security Centre guidelines, developed with international partners.

resources.title: Presidio documentation
resources.note: Getting started and reference for detecting and anonymising personal data.

stages.title: Governance and team guidance
stages.goal: Turn what you have learned into rules your team can follow without asking you each time.

gate.build: Draft a one-page AI use guideline for your team: what data may go into AI tools, who approves new uses, and how outputs are checked.
gate.check: Could a new team member follow it without asking you anything?

resources.title: AI playbook for the UK government
resources.note: Written for the UK public sector, and a good template for the principles any team needs.

resources.title: NIST AI risk management framework
resources.note: A voluntary framework from the US standards body for managing AI risk.

resources.title: NIST generative AI profile (AI 600-1)
resources.note: A companion profile that applies the framework to generative AI.

resources.title: OWASP GenAI security project
resources.note: OWASP's wider project on generative AI security, beyond the top 10 list.
